cards.title: Light
cards.plain: Where the light comes from and how hard it is. It decides the mood and how real the picture feels.
cards.example: A lamp on in the evening feels different from a bright window at noon.

options.label: Lamps and window
options.plain: Light from what is really in the room: a lamp, a window, a screen. Uneven, with dull corners.
options.example: A kitchen at 6pm with the ceiling light on and a grey window behind.

lighting.custom: mixed with dim window daylight, uneven, with some dull corners

options.label: Window daylight
options.plain: Soft daylight coming in from one side, with shade on the other.
options.example: Reading by a window on a cloudy morning.

lighting.custom: from a single window to one side

options.label: Cloudy day
options.plain: Even grey daylight with no hard shadows. Calm and plain.
options.example: A walk outside when the sky is a flat white.

options.label: Warm evening lamp
options.plain: Warm yellow light from a household lamp, with the rest of the room falling into dark.
options.example: A sofa corner with one table lamp on after dinner.

lighting.custom: a single household lamp, the far side of the room dim

options.label: Low sun
options.plain: Warm light from a sun low in the sky, with long shadows.
options.example: The hour before sunset when everything turns gold.

options.label: Phone flash
options.plain: A quick flash straight from the phone. Bright front, hard shadow behind.
options.example: A photo taken in a dark hallway at night.

look.lighting: direct on-camera phone flash, slightly harsh, with a hard small shadow behind the subject

cards.title: Camera
cards.plain: Where the camera stands and what it is. A plain phone shot looks like someone just took it.
cards.example: A photo from your pocket at chest height, not from a tripod.

options.label: Plain phone
options.plain: An ordinary phone camera held at normal height. A bit wide, nothing fancy.
options.example: A snapshot you send to a friend in the group chat.

camera.custom: shot on an ordinary phone camera, slightly wide lens, no depth-of-field tricks

options.label: Close, at eye level
options.plain: Near the subject, looking straight across at it.
options.example: Crouching down to look a cat in the face.

options.label: From above
options.plain: Held up high, looking down at the subject.
options.example: Leaning over a table to snap your lunch.

options.label: Down low
options.plain: Held near the floor, looking slightly up.
options.example: A photo taken from the pet's own height.

options.label: From the side
options.plain: The camera sees the subject side-on instead of face-on.
options.example: Catching someone walking past you.

cards.title: Framing
cards.plain: Where the subject sits in the picture. Off to one side feels caught, dead centre feels posed.
cards.example: A friend's snapshot with you a bit to the left, not a school portrait.

options.label: Off-centre snapshot
options.plain: The subject sits to one side, a little crooked, like it was caught rather than set up.
options.example: A photo taken quickly, with some empty floor on one side.

look.composition: off-centre and slightly crooked, framed like a quick candid snapshot with the subject away from the middle

options.label: Off to a third
options.plain: The subject sits on one of the lines that split the picture into three.
options.example: A person standing a third of the way in from the edge.

options.label: Room to move into
options.plain: Empty space in front of where the subject is looking or heading.
options.example: A dog trotting left with open path ahead of it.

options.label: Things in front and behind
options.plain: Something near, the subject in the middle, something far. It feels like a real place.
options.example: A chair arm in front, the subject, then a doorway behind.

options.label: Cropped by the edge
options.plain: The frame cuts off a bit of the subject, like a quick snap.
options.example: A photo where the tail or elbow is missing.

look.composition: cropped tight and a little careless, part of the subject cut off by the frame edge, like a quick snap

cards.title: Colour
cards.plain: How strong or soft the colours are. Real phone photos are rarely loud.
cards.example: A photo where the green is dull and the white is slightly yellow.

options.label: Muted and natural
options.plain: Soft, everyday colours as the phone saw them, with no heavy colour effect on top.
options.example: A holiday snapshot straight from your camera roll.

look.color: muted natural colours as a phone records them, no heavy colour grading, slightly flat contrast

options.label: Warm and faded
options.plain: Warm tones with slightly faded blacks, like an old print.
options.example: Photos in a family album from years ago.

options.label: Clean and bright
options.plain: Clear, bright colours that stay close to what your eyes saw.
options.example: A tidy product shot on a bright afternoon.

options.label: Rich and earthy
options.plain: Deep greens and warm browns, like a nature film.
options.example: A garden after rain.

options.label: Cool and grey
options.plain: Cooler, greyer colours that feel quiet and a bit cold.
options.example: A winter morning by the window.

look.color: cool grey-blue tones, low saturation, quiet and slightly cold

cards.title: Pose
cards.plain: What the subject is doing. Caught doing something feels real. Looking at the lens feels posed.
cards.example: Mid-laugh, turned to someone out of frame.

options.label: Caught mid-moment
options.plain: Doing something and not looking at the camera, as if no one was taking a picture.
options.example: Half-turned, busy with something else.

posing.custom: not looking at the camera, attention on something else

options.label: Moving
options.plain: Frozen halfway through a step or a turn.
options.example: A dog trotting across the room.

options.label: Glancing away
options.plain: Head turned toward something outside the picture.
options.example: Looking up because the door just opened.

look.posing: head turned, glancing at something off-frame, not at the camera

options.label: Real reaction
options.plain: A laugh or a surprised look caught half-way, not a held smile.
options.example: Someone laughing at a joke you missed.

options.label: Relaxed slouch
options.plain: Shoulders dropped, standing or sitting the way people do when no one is watching.
options.example: Leaning on the counter waiting for the kettle.

options.label: Resting
options.plain: Settled and loose, eyes half closed, not performing.
options.example: A cat stretched out on the sofa arm.

look.posing: resting loosely, weight settled, eyes half closed, not performing for the camera

options.label: Set down casually
options.plain: Left where someone put it, not lined up with the frame.
options.example: A bag dropped on a bench.

look.posing: set down casually, not squared up to the camera

options.label: At an angle
options.plain: Turned a little, so you see it from a corner and not head-on.
options.example: A mug with its handle pointing away.

look.posing: turned at a slight angle, seen from a corner rather than head-on

options.label: Just used
options.plain: It looks like someone was using it a moment ago.
options.example: A book left open, face down.

look.posing: looks as if it was just being used and left, nothing arranged for the picture

options.label: Half out of sight
options.plain: Partly tucked behind or under something else.
options.example: Keys peeking out from under a scarf.

look.posing: partly tucked behind or under something else in the scene, not fully on show

cards.title: Small details
cards.plain: The little untidy things that real life has. They are what makes a picture feel lived in.
cards.example: A hair out of place, a crease in a sleeve, a mug left on the side.

options.label: Real wear
options.plain: Scuffs and marks only where things really wear: edges, handles, folds and corners.
options.example: The worn patch on a shoe, where it always bends.

look.evidence: wear only where things really wear: edges, handles, folds and corners, small scuffs and marks

options.label: Everyday clutter
options.plain: A few ordinary things left lying around the place.
options.example: A charger cable, a mug and a jacket over a chair.

look.evidence: a few everyday things left lying about, such as a charger cable, a mug and a jacket over a chair

options.label: Uneven fur
options.plain: Fur that clumps and sticks up in places, with a little dust in it.
options.example: A cat's coat after a nap, flat on one side.

options.label: Whiskers and nose
options.plain: One whisker bent, a damp nose catching light.
options.example: A dog's nose just after it licked it.

options.label: Real skin
options.plain: Visible pores, fine lines and small marks, and a slightly uneven skin tone.
options.example: Look closely at a friend's cheek in daylight.

look.evidence: visible pores, fine lines, small marks and an uneven skin tone, true to real skin

options.label: Stray hairs
options.plain: A few loose hairs sticking out and hair flattened on one side.
options.example: Hair after wearing a hat.

evidence.custom: a few flyaway hairs catching the light

options.label: Creased clothes
options.plain: Folds and creases in clothes where the body bends them.
options.example: A shirt crumpled at the elbow after a day of sitting.

evidence.custom: creases in the clothing at the elbows and waist

options.label: Dust and fingerprints
options.plain: A thin film of dust and a fingerprint or two where hands really touch.
options.example: A glass table the day after a party.

look.evidence: a thin film of dust, faint scuffs and a fingerprint or two where hands really touch

options.label: Just handled
options.plain: Small signs that someone picked it up and put it back a moment ago.
options.example: A lid not quite square after you opened the jar.

look.evidence: small signs it was just handled, a lid or cushion slightly out of square, one thing nudged out of line
